title: Review Assistant
summary: A bounded assistant that helps benefits caseworkers locate supporting policy passages while preserving human decisions and uncertainty.
intended_users: Public-benefit caseworkers reviewing complex eligibility documents with accountable human sign-off.

design_decisions.problem_or_constraint: Caseworkers spend time locating policy while automated eligibility decisions would create unacceptable harm.
design_decisions.alternatives_considered: Rules-only search missed paraphrases. Unbounded chat was rejected for hallucination and authority ambiguity.
design_decisions.chosen_approach_and_rationale: Use retrieval-bounded drafting with mandatory citations, abstention, and human disposition.
design_decisions.accepted_trade_off: The assistant cannot answer outside the indexed policy set and adds review steps.
design_decisions.validation_approach: Tests cover missing citations, low-confidence abstention, prohibited decision language, user rejection, and audit events. A separate qualitative set is documented but not claimed as runtime proof.
design_decisions.reconsideration_conditions: Remove generation if citation precision or harmful-completion rates miss the published pilot thresholds.

testing_strategy: Pytest cases cover citation presence, abstention thresholds, prohibited decisions, rejection, and audit logging. Blinded domain review remains required.
security_threat: A plausible but unsupported model statement influences a benefits decision. Source allowlists, citation requirements, abstention, prohibited-action rules, visible uncertainty, and human disposition prevent autonomous decisions. Residual risk: Caseworker automation bias remains possible and retrieval quality can omit relevant policy.
production_limitation: Only the frozen policy corpus is searchable; multilingual quality and real workflow latency remain unverified.
technical_debt: Expand the expert-reviewed calibration set and add subgroup error analysis before any live pilot.
track_alignment_explanation: AI is essential but bounded to retrieval and drafting for a defined high-stakes workflow, with human agency, uncertainty, data minimization, and a documented simpler baseline.

ai_disclosure.purposes: Codex was used to author this deliberately synthetic calibration fixture and its structured submission answers.
ai_disclosure.substantially_generated_areas: All fixture source, documentation, tests, and submission narratives are synthetic and AI-assisted.
ai_disclosure.review_validation: The calibration operator reviews files for intended evidence strength, consistency, and absence of real secrets before pinning the commit.
ai_disclosure.rejected_or_changed_suggestion: Generic claims of runtime correctness were rejected because Finch performs static evidence review only.

ai_disclosure_narrative: This entire project is synthetic AI-assisted test data. It represents no participant, deployed product, or real credential.
